transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Janelle Brooks (CISO, Acme), Tom Nguyen (Security Engineer, Acme), Priya Rao (IT Ops, Acme)

Summary: quick security & compliance sync to walk through latest pen test results, discuss vulnerability management and patch cadence, confirm secure SDLC practices and KMS/encryption posture, and agree next steps for remediation POA and follow-up.

Topics: pen test findings (high/med/low), CVSS triage, vulnerability mgmt pipeline, patching cadence (monthly vs quarterly), secure SDLC / code review gating, SOC 2 / ISO evidence, RBAC/SSO and audit logging, KMS/HSM and data residency requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, I think we all have the pen test summary in front of us, i will hand it over to carlos for the technical run thru.
[00:16] Carlos: yeah thanks maya, hi janelle, tom, priya. so quick note, first page is executive summary - overall a few high-severity findings, most are medium, a number of low config issues. the critical one flagged was an unauth RCE vector on image upload in a legacy endpoint - looks like it ties back to insufficient sanitization in the image service.
[00:38] Tom: yeah that one was surprising — it's in our legacy thumbnails service, we thought it was behind auth but pen tester found a path via CDN caching that bypasses the token, so it's essentially an auth bypass combined with risky deserialization.
[00:58] Janelle: can you remind me the CVSS score on that?
[01:03] Carlos: they scored it 9.1, so high. there are also two medium findings around outdated dependencies in the model inference pipeline container images — openssl and a libimage lib that need patching / rebuild.
[01:21] Priya: the container images are built in our CI, we patch monthly but some images slipped last quarter. question: does redwood have any specifics about image scanning or recommended base images?
[01:36] Maya: yeah we do; carlos i'll share Redwood's hardened base images and our image scanning checklist. we also recommend signing images and using your registry's vulnerability scanning; we'll send those links after call.
[01:49] Carlos: right; Redwood's guidance is to run SBOM generation, scan with a vuln scanner at build time, and gate deploys on no critical findings. for inference runtime we also recommend quantized model image builds with minimal libs to reduce attack surface.
[02:08] Tom: sounds good. on the auth bypass, can redwood help with proof-of-concept mitigation patterns? e.g. token validation at edge or stricter CDN rules?
[02:19] Carlos: absolutely. we can provide both config changes (edge token validation / require signed URLs) and code-level mitigations. i'll draft a recommended fix that you can apply as a quick patch and then a longer-term remediation for the service architecture.
[02:34] Janelle: shifting gears to encryption — we had a question about KMS usage for key rotation and HSM backing. is redwood using customer-managed keys or a hosted KMS?
[02:45] Maya: for hosted customers we support Redwood-managed KMS by default, and for Dedicated / Private we can integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM, or on-prem HSM) — we have docs on key rotation and access policies. i'll send the doc bundle.
[02:58] Priya: and logs — audit logs need to be tamper-evident and retained for 1 year for our compliance. does redwood provide immutable audit logs and export to our SIEM?
[03:10] Carlos: yes we export audit trails (API calls, auth events, admin actions) with tamper-evidence via checksum and can stream to your SIEM (syslog/Kafka/Cloud). retention is configurable; for Dedicated/Private you can set longer retention and S3 lifecycle.
[03:25] Tom: do you include token-level metadata so we can map requests to internal user ids? we need per-token cost and latency breakdown too for QA.
[03:33] Maya: yes token metadata is in the trace, and Console exposes per-route metrics. we'll add a doc link to how to map user ids to tokens in audit logs.
[03:44] Janelle: SOC 2 artifacts — we need evidence around secure SDLC and patching cadence, what do you have available?
[03:52] Maya: we have our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certification artifacts, plus our secure SDLC policy (code review rules, static analysis, dependency scanning, PR gating) and patch management policy. i'll share the bundle.
[04:05] Carlos: to expand on SDLC, we run SAST on PRs, dependency scanning on CI, and require two approvers for security-sensitive changes. patch cadence: critical patches pushed immediately, regular security patch window monthly, and major infra upgrades quarterly.
[04:21] Priya: what's your patching SLA for critical vulnerabilities? we need to show our risk committee timelines.
[04:28] Carlos: critical CVEs, we aim for 48-72 hours to mitigation or compensating control, followed by permanent fix in next patch window. medium are typically within 2 weeks; low within the next monthly cycle.
[04:40] Tom: do you run external pen tests regularly and how do you track regressions?
[04:46] Maya: we run an annual third-party pen test and quarterly internal red-team exercises; findings are tracked in our vuln management tracker (we'll share a sanitized export). we also run regression tests against our infra after patching.
[05:00] Janelle: what about CVE disclosure and notification — will redwood notify customers if something affects their deployment?
[05:06] Carlos: yes we have an incident notification process; customers on Dedicated/Private get prioritized notifications with recommended mitigations and timelines. hosted customers get notifications via the console and email.
[05:18] Tom: on remediation ownership, for Dedicated setups, do you patch the runtime or we patch our images?
[05:25] Maya: for Dedicated, the infra/software stack is managed by Redwood with agreed OS/kernel patch windows; for customer-managed images we provide guidance and patches for our agents and runtime, but customers typically rebuild app images. we'll define ownership in the SRT (service runbook) for your account.
[05:42] Priya: data residency — we need EU-only residency for some workloads; can Redwood guarantee region residency and provide proof?
[05:50] Carlos: yes, Dedicated or Private can be pinned to specific regions, and we produce exportable data residency attestations and logs showing data location. for hosted multi-tenant, we can route requests to EU region but the control plane may be in another region; if you need full residency, Private/VPC is recommended.
[06:10] Janelle: RBAC and SSO — we require SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC with admin separation. what's available?
[06:19] Maya: we support SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC with roles + custom roles for route-level permissions. audit logs capture admin role changes and console actions.
[06:30] Tom: any caveats around service accounts or token expiry?
[06:33] Carlos: service tokens can be short-lived or long-lived per your policy, and we recommend rotating and scoping them to least privilege. tokens are tied to key ids in KMS so you can revoke access quickly.
[06:47] Priya: curious about vulnerability management lifecycle — do you have an SLA or cadence for vulnerability validation once a ticket is created?
[06:55] Maya: once a vuln ticket is created, SE triages within 24 hours, assigns severity, then engineering owner provides POA and ETA. we'll share our vuln triage runbook.
[07:08] Tom: for the image CVEs, will you accept CVE exceptions if mitigated by compensating controls? we need that flexibility for certain third-party libs.
[07:17] Carlos: yes CVE exceptions can be documented with compensating controls; they go through a security review board and are timeboxed. acceptance requires evidence of mitigation and monitoring.
[07:30] Janelle: let's talk about evidence for our audit — we need proof of patch windows over past 12 months and change logs.
[07:39] Maya: we can provide patch logs, deploy timelines, and the SOC 2 evidence pack which includes those artifacts. i'll include a redacted history for your auditors.
[07:50] Priya: quick question on telemetry retention — logs are heavy, can we set different retention for dev vs prod?
[07:57] Carlos: yes retention is configurable per environment for Dedicated/Private; for hosted there's a standard retention tier and optional extended retention add-on.
[08:09] Tom: regarding the RCE finding, any suggested immediate mitigations?
[08:13] Carlos: immediate steps: 1) disable the vulnerable endpoint or put strict auth at the edge; 2) block problematic content types at CDN; 3) deploy WAF rule to block known exploit patterns; 4) patch deserialization library. quick wins are edge auth and WAF.
[08:32] Janelle: ok let's make those action items, Tom to own short-term fixes.
[08:36] Tom: yep I'll take it.
[08:38] Maya: we'll also run a focused scan from our end against your staging to validate.
[08:44] Carlos: one more note — we observed a few misconfigurations in audit log permissions where logs were writeable by a service account; recommend locking down S3 bucket policies and enabling object lock for critical logs.
[09:00] Priya: will do.
[09:02] Janelle: any other high-level risks called out?
[09:05] Carlos: mostly configuration drift and some outdated deps. no supply-chain compromise indicators at this time.
[09:12] Tom: on the outdated dependency items, is the suggested path rebuild images with patched base or apply in-place yum/apt patches?
[09:21] Carlos: rebuild images for immutable infra; in-place patches are ok for short-term but rebuild + redeploy is cleaner.
[09:29] Maya: okay wrapping up, quick recap of owners and next steps: maya to send SOC2/ISO and sanitized pen test report; carlos to provide mitigation checklist and image hardening guidance; tom to produce prioritized POA; priya to confirm residency and region list.
[09:48] Janelle: thanks everyone — timeline for POA by 2025-06-24 works for us.
[09:54] Maya: perfect. we'll schedule the follow-up week of 6/30 to review remediation.
[09:59] Tom: thanks.
[10:01] Carlos: thanks all.

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard terms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash), and product names had minor typos in the automated transcript.

Attachments / references mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security/soc2 (SOC 2 bundle link placeholder), https://redwood.example.com/docs/security/kms (KMS/HSM integration guide), sanitized-pen-test-summary (shared link post-call), vuln-tracker-export (sanitized link).

End of transcript.
